text.title: Motion and Micro-Interaction System Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether duration and easing tokens have a path into code, how much surface the spec must bind, and whether anyone can reject a component that hard-codes its timings — separating one-off choreography from a governed motion token system.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a path by which duration and easing tokens actually reach code — CSS custom properties, a Style Dictionary build, Figma variables, or a platform theme file?

branch.when: no token pipeline exists; timings live as millisecond literals inside component stylesheets

conclusion.verdict: skip; the scale has no way to reach code — build the token distribution path first, then publish the duration and easing tiers into it

branch.when: a token build exists and components already consume tokens by name
branch.question: How much surface does this spec have to bind?

branch.when: a single page or a single animated component

conclusion.verdict: skip; specify the choreography inline on the component — a closed token scale for one component is overhead

branch.when: a component library or a product-wide motion language across many surfaces
branch.question: Can a governance owner reject a component that hard-codes its own timings, and does any component's JavaScript depend on animationend, animationiteration or transitionend?

branch.when: no owner or gate can reject a hard-coded timing

conclusion.verdict: skip for now; an unenforced closed scale is documentation — establish design-system-governance ownership and a lint rule first

branch.when: an owner and a lint or review gate exist, and component JavaScript listens for animation or transition completion events

conclusion.verdict: apply, but pin the reduced-motion override before anything else; never animation: none or transition: none on those elements — use a 0.01 ms duration with iteration-count 1, or an explicit non-animated path firing the same state change

branch.when: an owner and a gate exist, and no component depends on animation completion events

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; closed named duration scale mapped to interaction class, three directional easing tokens with linear reserved for indeterminate indicators, reduced motion replacing displacement rather than shortening it, transform and opacity only
